hints.title: All-Pairs Shortest Path Obstacle
hints.text: Finding the city that reaches the fewest neighbors within distance threshold requires calculating shortest paths between all pairs of cities. How can repeated single-source shortest path relaxation determine neighbor counts?

hints.title: All-Pairs Distance Threshold Invariant
hints.text: Running Dijkstra or Floyd-Warshall computes the exact minimum distance between every pair of cities. A neighbor j is reachable from i if dist[i][j] <= distanceThreshold.

hints.title: Shortest Path Neighbor Counting Procedure
hints.text: For each city i from 0 to n - 1, run Dijkstra to compute shortest distances to all other cities. Count distinct cities j other than i with distance at most distanceThreshold. Track city with minimum reachable count, preferring larger city index in ties.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: E: number of bidirectional edges (E <= V * (V - 1) / 2)
complexity.notes: Running Dijkstra from each of the V vertices takes O(V * E log V) time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Unbounded branch search explores sub-optimal paths exceeding distance threshold repeatedly.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Adjacency graph consumes O(V + E) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Breaking ties by choosing the city with the greater numerical index.
